live.instructions: eulaw.ai serves European legislation and case law with the identifiers and source URLs needed to cite it. Search it whenever an answer depends on what a European law says or how a court applied it, rather than answering from recollection. Scope every search to jurisdiction codes returned by list_jurisdictions. Quote and cite the retrieved text, keep each document's identifiers and URL with the claim they support, and say so plainly when a search returns nothing rather than filling the gap.

tools.name: search_legal_sources
tools.title: Search European legal sources
tools.description: Semantic search over eulaw.ai's corpus of European legislation and case law. Use it whenever a question turns on what a European or national European law actually says, or on how a court has applied it, and you need the authoritative text rather than recollection. Returns one entry per matching document: title, jurisdiction, document type, publication date, the identifiers that document carries (CELEX, ELI, ECLI where they apply), a source URL, an opaque document_id, and a passage from the document. It returns passages, not whole documents - call get_document with the document_id when the surrounding text matters. It cannot answer about jurisdictions outside the covered set: call list_jurisdictions first if you do not already know which codes are covered. It is not a general web search and holds no material outside the legal corpus.

query.description: What to search for, as a natural-language description of the legal question or subject matter. Matching is semantic, so a full question works better than isolated keywords. Query in the language of the jurisdiction being searched where possible: the corpus is stored in each source's own language, and a query in another language matches it only through translation.

jurisdictions.description: Which jurisdictions to search, as the codes returned by list_jurisdictions. Required - there is no all-jurisdictions search. At most 15 per call.

only_in_force.description: When true, drop documents whose expiry date has passed, so only currently applicable law is returned. Leave false (the default) when legislative history, superseded versions or the state of the law at some earlier time is part of the question. Setting it costs additional lookup time.

tools.name: get_document
tools.title: Read a legal document
tools.description: Fetch the text of a single document from the eulaw.ai corpus by the document_id and jurisdiction that search_legal_sources returned for it. Use it when a passage from search is not enough to answer accurately - to read the provision around a quoted fragment, to check a definition, or to confirm wording before relying on it. Documents can be long, so it returns a slice: the response states the total length and whether more remains, and offset pages through the rest. It takes only identifiers this server issued; it cannot fetch a document from a URL or a citation.

document_id.description: The document_id from a search_legal_sources result. Opaque - do not construct one.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction code the document was returned under.

offset.description: Character offset to start reading from (default 0). Use it to continue past a truncated slice.

max_chars.description: How many characters to return (default 20000, maximum 50000).

tools.name: list_jurisdictions
tools.title: List covered jurisdictions
tools.description: List the jurisdiction codes this server can search, with their names. Call it before the first search of a conversation, or whenever a question names a country whose coverage you have not confirmed, so the search is scoped to codes that exist rather than guessed ones. Coverage changes as jurisdictions are added, so treat the returned list as current and do not assume a code is covered because it was covered before.
